newsitem.title: FRANCE: French deficit above 3.5 percent - minister quoted.
newsitem.headline: French deficit above 3.5 percent - minister quoted.

text.p: Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn was quoted as telling a parliamentary committee on Wednesday that a key audit due next week would show a deficit above 3.5 percent of gross domestic product this year.

"The audit of public finances, which will show the budget deficit above the 3.5 percent mark, will reduce the margin for manoeuvre," official minutes released after the closed-door session paraphrased Strauss-Kahn as saying.
Socialist Lionel Jospin commissioned the audit soon after being elected on June 1, partly to help decide what measures are necessary for France to join a single European currency.

The results of the audit are being watched closely to see how far the government is prepared to go to bring the deficit towards three percent of gross domestic product needed to qualify for European monetary union, scheduled to start in 1999.

Many expect it to target a deficit level of some 3.3 percent of GDP, above the 3.0 percent forecast by the previous centre-right government, but below the 3.5 percent or so expected to be estimated by the audit.

The government may also announce on Monday after the release of the audit that it plans to curb the deficit further next year to three percent of GDP in order to allay fears among its European partners about the overshoot this year.
